traceability.notes:
All defined requirements and acceptance criteria for Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION are implemented and verified.
• Core validation logic: The ESLint rule `valid-annotation-format` (src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts) plus its helpers implement syntax and format checks for `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` annotations. `validateStoryAnnotation` and `validateReqAnnotation` enforce patterns for story paths and requirement IDs, including missing-value vs invalid-value distinctions.
• Requirements coverage: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION & REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: The rule’s `meta`, schema, and `create`/Program visitor scan all comments and apply consistent validation using shared helpers. Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly tag these requirements and verify behavior. - REQ-PATH-FORMAT: Story paths are validated against a default or configured regex. Invalid extensions, missing extensions, and path traversal (`../`) are all detected and reported, with auto-fix for suffix-only issues. This is covered by multiple `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT]` tests. - REQ-REQ-FORMAT: Requirement IDs are validated against `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$` (or configured pattern). Missing IDs and malformed IDs like `invalid-format` are reported with specific messages; tests `[REQ-REQ-FORMAT]` assert these. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: PendingAnnotation state and `collapseAnnotationValue` support annotations split across multiple lines in block/JSDoc comments. Tests cover valid and invalid multi-line story/req values and ensure correct handling of whitespace and termination. - REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: `normalizeCommentLine` and `isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine` support inline annotations, JSDoc leading `*`, and various whitespace layouts, and coexist correctly with other JSDoc tags. Valid tests with JSDoc-style comments and the JSDoc coexistence tests confirm this behavior. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: Error messages are constructed via `buildStoryErrorMessage` / `buildReqErrorMessage` and surfaced through `meta.messages.invalidStoryFormat` / `invalidReqFormat`. The tests assert the exact `details` strings, including echoing the offending value and a concrete example; documentation mirrors these messages.
• Acceptance criteria: - Core Functionality: Demonstrated by the rule implementation and comprehensive RuleTester coverage for both `@story` and `@req` (and reuse of the same rules for `@supports`). - Quality Standards: Rule follows ESLint best practices (meta/docs/messages/schema/fixable) and is integrated through the plugin index and flat-config presets; tests use `RuleTester` with proper parser options. - Integration: The plugin’s recommended/strict configs enable `valid-annotation-format` together with `require-story-annotation` and `require-branch-annotation`, so it validates the same annotations those rules require. It operates purely on comments, making it compatible with existing detection rules. - User Experience & Error Handling: Messages are clear and specific for different failure modes (missing vs invalid story/req, config regex errors), and the code includes careful handling of malformed comments, invalid regex configuration (falling back to defaults while reporting `invalidRuleConfiguration`), multi-line edge cases, and JSDoc boundaries. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md provides a full format specification, configuration options, and examples of valid and invalid annotations that align with the story’s examples.
All related tests pass under `npm test -- --verbose`, including the dedicated suite for this rule, so the story is fully implemented and verified.
